title: Recordings and sounds in a document sit on the Library shelf and drag onto the timeline
goal: The video mock fills the Library with the clips and sounds you brought in (b-roll.mov, music) and drops a first clip by dragging a Library tile onto a track. Today the Library only holds pictures, so the only way to put b-roll on the timeline is from the Finder. Put every recording and sound the document holds on the Library shelf, and let a tile be dragged onto a track the same way a file from the Finder is.
notes: Filed by bring-in-a-second-clip-and-cut-between-clips (2026-09-23). The timeline drop is TimelineFileDropDelegate + EditorState+TimelineDrop (dropTimelineFile takes a URL; a tile should hand the same landing a MovieRef/SoundRef it already holds rather than a file). DocumentMedia.swift lists pictures only; MovieRef/SoundRef live on layers (layer.movie, content .sound). Mock: docs/design/mocks/pages/video.html lines ~326-327 and ~547 (libtile b-roll.mov), ~695. Walk step dropOnTimeline shows how a walk aims at a track and a second.
acceptance: A recording or sound brought into a video document appears as a tile on the Library shelf with its name and length, as video.html draws b-roll.mov 0:04
Dragging that tile onto a track lands it at the moment and on the track under the pointer, with the same ghost, snapping and command-key insert as a file from the Finder
The mock onboarding step Drop a first clip (drag a tile from Library onto an empty track) works at Next defaults
A walk at defaults drags a Library tile onto V1 and claims where it landed

log.note: Pre-build review: (1) Today the shelf is derived from layers only, so a clip's FRAME showed up as a picture tile and deleting the last clip of b-roll would take it off the shelf, unlike a Premiere bin. So the document gets a media pool (document.media) that remembers every recording/sound brought in, by file name (b-roll.mov as the mock captions it); the shelf is pool + anything on the timeline never remembered. (2) The shelf is height-capped and tile height is arithmetic (LibraryShelfLayout), so the length goes as a corner badge in the thumbnail (where Premiere's icon view puts duration) rather than a second caption line as video.html draws it: listed as a mock difference in the audit. (3) A tile drag hands over the file itself (own-process file URL), so the timeline lands it through exactly the Finder path: same ghost, snapping, cmd-insert, and MovieLibrary returns the same ref for the same file so nothing is read twice. Own-process only, so a tile can never be dropped on the Finder and move the user's source file. (4) Filling the Library by dropping a file ON the panel (mock step 2) is not in this task's acceptance; checking the queue before filing.

Built: document media pool (PhotonzDocument.media, rememberMedia; DocumentClipMedia.swift, 13 tests) remembered on every timeline landing, canvas clip drop, Add Sound and recording open; DocumentMedia.clips lists pool then unremembered timeline media; clip layers no longer show as picture tiles. LibraryClipTile.swift: poster frame or mock green waveform well, length corner badge, drag hands over the file URL own-process so the timeline lands it through the Finder path; double click, right-click Add at Playhead and the picked section's Add at Playhead all go through placeLibraryPick -> placeTimelineFileAtPlayhead (overwrite on the one picked track, else a new track). Harness: dropOnTimeline takes tile instead of file (parse tests added); pickFirstMedia picks clips first.

Walk library-clip-onto-a-track-walk at defaults (View > Library via showLibrary, no flag): ok, 7 real window captures. Tile onto EMPTY Audio track lands at 1.00s; recording tile snaps onto V1 end at 8.00s; cmd-insert at 3s pushes along; undo; Add at Playhead overwrites 2-10s on V1.

Follow-ups: filed recordings-and-sounds-can-go-into-the-library-wi (p1, mock step Fill the Library: Import / drop on panel); filed a-video-document-shows-the-library-in-its-dock with a decision card (Library hidden until View > Library per the user's own rule vs the mock's always-present group). Left rough, not filed: (1) on a long video dock the picked tile's own section lands below the fold, the same as a picked picture tile does; (2) 68pt tiles cut longer file names in the middle (in the audit's rough, user can react); (3) a movie with its sound detached counts both layers as uses.
